rows.evidence: Q1: Conditions, materials and methods and Results and Discussion - three-year (2013-2015) field experiments at KazNIIZiR demonstration plots near Almaty on light-chestnut soil comparing furrow irrigation, surface and subsurface drip with and without mulch film, sowing patterns, fertilizer and irrigation regimes, with weed counts, biomass and yield recorded in three replications.
rows.notes: The study does report its own weed counts, but the 8-10-fold reduction is attributed to the mulch film, not to drip irrigation: in options with mulch film weeds numbered 18-23 plants/m2, while in all options without mulch film (which include surface and subsurface drip as well as the furrow control) weed numbers reached up to 165 plants/m2; the conclusion explicitly states that cultivation under mulch film at drip irrigation reduces weed infestation 8-10 times versus control. No separate weed counts are given for drip without mulch versus furrow, so there is no evidence that drip per se reduces weeds relative to surface irrigation. Weed results are reported only as ranges without replication-level dispersion statistics, no triangulation (visual/manual counts only), single site, single crop, plot scale, and no stated limitations of the weed result.

notes: Full text appears complete. The weed-infestation result is a mulch-film effect under drip (mulch vs no mulch), which the review passage misattributes to drip irrigation versus surface irrigation. Yield and economic results are reported per treatment but weed counts are given only as pooled ranges for mulch vs no-mulch options.
